source.title: Curriculum Loss: Robust Learning and Generalization against Label Corruption

record.tranche_reason: Reports test accuracy for standard networks under several label-corruption conditions, bearing on the noisy-label generalization part of V4; it does not measure random-label fitting or the other versions' outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses deep networks memorizing wrong labels and cites Zhang et al. (2017), but that cited result is not this study's result. Its own results include standard-network test accuracies under corruption; it does not report standard-network training error for those conditions.
record.test_reason: The study's own standard-training results test the generalization component of V4: test accuracy decreases between 20% and 50% symmetric corruption on three datasets. They do not test perfect training-set fitting or degradation over the full corruption range.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical conclusion. More fully, the authors prove upper-bound properties of curriculum loss, extend it to noise-pruned curriculum loss for heavier corruption, and report robustness on benchmark datasets. They do not independently establish random-label memorization or clean-before-noise learning.
record.recipe_differences: Uses curriculum and noise-pruned curriculum losses, with comparisons to standard network training; studies robustness to partial label corruption rather than the original random-label memorization intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies across dataset and corruption type/rate in the reported standard-network results.

fits_no_version.finding: NPCL improves noisy-label test accuracy and selects cleaner training subsets relative to competing methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive sample pruning can improve generalization under partial label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix I reports 100% training accuracy for soft hinge loss with Adam and SGD, and hard hinge loss with SGD, on CIFAR100; label corruption is not specified for this experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss smoothing and optimizer choice affect optimization on CIFAR100.

record.problems: Standard-network rows report test accuracy only, without corresponding training error. The noise settings are symmetric or pair flipping at specified partial rates, not a fully random labeling of the training set.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training settings relative to true labels.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect fitting of corrupted training labels; steady degradation throughout the zero-to-total-corruption range; the chance endpoint; and simultaneous signal learning and noise memorization. A single pair-flip rate cannot establish a trend.
Effects of adding or removing explicit regularization on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Direct measurement of clean patterns being learned before noisy labels. This ordering motivates sample pruning but is attributed to Arpit et al., rather than independently measured.

missing.what: Standard cross-entropy test-accuracy comparisons on Tiny-ImageNet with 20% and 50% symmetric noise provide another setting for V4's generalization component. The supplied text contains no readable curve values, so their direction and magnitude cannot be determined.

record.verdict_notes: Observed states for symmetric-noise rows refer only to the measured test-error component of V4, assessed jointly across rates. Missing training-error measurements are untested components, not evidence against V4. Section 3.2 explicitly attributes the Softmax, RoG, and D2L numbers in Tables 1–3 to Lee et al.; these are not additional results produced by this study.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, training error, chance test error, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Whether training error remains perfect; whether networks capture remaining signal while memorizing noise. The reported test-accuracy rows do not establish these.
Whether regularization or augmentation prevents random-label fitting, or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Whether networks learn real-label patterns before memorizing noise, and whether the learning dynamics differ.

rows.subject: Standard
rows.operation_detail: Trained under symmetric label flipping at 20% noise; reports average test accuracy over the last ten epochs.
rows.note: Test accuracy does not establish whether training error was perfect.
rows.check: Correct value. Together with R2, establishes the predicted test-error increase over the tested rates; perfect training accuracy remains unmeasured.

relationships.condition: Standard CNN training on MNIST, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100; symmetric corruption increased from 20% to 50%; generalization component only.
relationships.reason: Accuracy decreases from 93.78% to 65.81% (R1–R2), 76.62% to 49.92% (R4–R5), and 47.05% to 25.47% (R7–R8), supporting increasing test error over these two rates.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy fell from 93.78% to 65.81% on MNIST, 76.62% to 49.92% on CIFAR10, and 47.05% to 25.47% on CIFAR100.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
